stem: Observe the series: 3, 10, 29, 66, 127, ?. The third difference of consecutive terms is constant. Find the 6th term.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Uses T(n) = n^3 - n + 3 giving 6^3 - 6 + 3 = 213; or approximates and rounds down to 210 by misreading the constant offset.
Correctly identifies T(n) = n^3 + 2 but computes 6^3 as 212 through a multiplication slip (6^3 = 6x6x6 = 216, not 212), giving 214.
Computes n^3 for n=6 as 216 but forgets to add the constant +2 offset extracted from the residuals, giving only 216.
Third differences are constant at 6, confirming a cubic T(n) = n^3 + c. Subtracting n^3 from each term gives residual 2 for all n. So T(n) = n^3 + 2 and T(6) = 216 + 2 = 218.

explanation: Compute first differences: 7, 19, 37, 61. Second differences: 12, 18, 24. Third differences: 6, 6 - constant, confirming a pure cubic. Subtracting n^3 from each term: 3-1=2, 10-8=2, 29-27=2, 66-64=2, 127-125=2. The residual is always 2, so T(n) = n^3 + 2. For n=6: 6^3 + 2 = 216 + 2 = 218.

explanation_sections.punchline: Constant third differences identify a cubic; stripping n^3 exposes a constant residual of 2, giving T(n) = n^3 + 2 and T(6) = 218.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: (1) differences: 7, 19, 37, 61; (2) second differences: 12, 18, 24; (3) third differences: 6, 6 - constant at 6, so leading coefficient a = 6/6 = 1; (4) subtract n^3 from each term: all residuals = 2; (5) T(n) = n^3 + 2; (6) T(6) = 216 + 2 = 218.
explanation_sections.lesson: Constant k-th differences signal a degree-k polynomial. Strip the leading n^k term and inspect the residuals to recover the lower-degree part.
explanation_sections.timing: 90-120 seconds. Three-level difference table is the unavoidable work. The traps are forgetting the +2 offset (giving 216) or a slip in computing 6^3.
